title: Minor leukocyte fractions do not establish added log-CRP prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: Eosinophil and basophil percentages are omitted from common leukocyte ratio summaries. We fitted fixed weighted spline-ridge models in 4,385 NHANES 2005–2006 adults and evaluated them without target refitting in 5,646 adults from the separately sampled 2009–2010 release. Adding minor fractions to age, BMI, sex, race/ethnicity, WBC, NLR, MLR and platelet count changed weighted log-CRP MSE from 1.1985742 to 1.1982641. Gain was 0.0003101, conditional rescaled-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [-0.0045929, 0.0055457], and source/target coefficient-refit uncertainty included zero. All five source cross-validation folds worsened; normal-WBC, stronger blood-index and absolute-major-cell controls reversed the tiny target gain. This is a scoped negative test, not equivalence or evidence against all differential-cell information. Separate same-program samples do not establish independent-study transport; prior CRP use in these releases also prevents calling this pristine confirmation.

citations.reason: Primary comparison of conventional immune markers motivated the question, not a replication of its mortality analysis.
